id: Matched: LPS-regulated GPCR expression in mouse macrophages
abstract: This study analyzed GPCR expression in mouse macrophages, comparing it to other cell types and LPS-stimulated macrophages. Several P2RY family members showed macrophage-specific expression or LPS-regulated changes, suggesting roles in macrophage biology and inflammation.

title: Metabolite-sensing GPCRs controlling interactions between adipose tissue and inflammation
authors: Elaine M. Duncan; Luca Vita; Bethany Dibnah; Brian D. Hudson
abstract: This paper reviews metabolite-sensing GPCRs in adipose tissue and their role in inflammation. These receptors, activated by fatty acids, hydroxy carboxylic acids, and succinate, are critical for metabolic-immune interactions.

title: Hydroxycarboxylic acid receptor 2 (HCAR2/GPR109A) expression and signaling promotes the maintenance of an immunoinhibitory retinal environment
authors: Folami L. Powell, Amany Tawfik, Pachiappan Arjunan, Deeksha Gambhir Chopra, Mohamed Al-Shabrawey, Na...
abstract: HCAR2/GPR109A expression was studied in retinal cells and its role in immune regulation investigated. HCAR2/GPR109A activation promotes an immunoinhibitory retinal environment, potentially protecting against degenerative diseases.

abstract: Activated niacin receptor HCA2 was studied in macrophages to understand its role in inflammation. Niacin inhibits macrophage migration via Gβγ/PKC/ERK1/2 signaling and receptor desensitization, protecting against septic shock.

title: Biological Roles and Therapeutic Potential of Hydroxy-Carboxylic Acid Receptors
authors: Kashan Ahmed
abstract: Hydroxy-carboxylic acid receptors (HCARs) are activated by metabolic intermediates and expressed in adipose tissue. They regulate lipolysis and represent promising therapeutic targets for metabolic diseases.

title: Macrophage Polarization: Different Gene Signatures in M1(LPS+) vs. Classically and M2(LPS–) vs. Alternatively Activated Macrophages
authors: Marco Orecchioni, Yanal Ghosheh, Akula Bala Pramod, Klaus Ley
abstract: This study compared gene expression in *in vivo* M1/M2 macrophages with *in vitro* classically/alternatively activated macrophages. The findings indicate that *in vivo* M1/M2 polarization is not equivalent to *in vitro* activation states.

title: The hydroxycarboxylic acid receptor HCA2 is required for the protective effect of ketogenic diet in epilepsy
authors: Jill C. Richardson; Guy A. Higgins; Neil Upton; Peter Massey; Mark Cunningham; Steve Wilson; Joerg H...
abstract: This study investigated the role of the HCA2 receptor in the ketogenic diet's anti-seizure effects. The HCA2 receptor is essential for the diet's protective benefits, suggesting it's a potential therapeutic target for epilepsy.

authors: Leah Elson; Niels Eijkelkamp; J. Henk Coert
abstract: This systematic review synthesized evidence for a conserved lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-mediated pathogenic mechanism across diverse tissues and evaluated its potential relevance to peripheral neuropathy

abstract: Histone deacetylase 2 (HDAC2) is essential for LPS-induced inflammatory responses in macrophages. HDAC2 regulates these responses by deacetylating c-Jun, which then represses pro-inflammatory gene transcription.

abstract: Houttuynia cordata extract reduces inflammatory cytokine production and modulates key signaling pathways in LPS-stimulated macrophages. It also shifts macrophages towards an anti-inflammatory phenotype, particularly when administered after inflammation begins. These findings suggest therapeutic potential for inflammatory diseases.

abstract: This study assessed the stability of eight common reference genes in LPS-stimulated murine macrophages. It found that some traditional genes are unreliable, and identified two new, stable reference genes for accurate gene expression analysis.
